articles.headline: SC 7-Judge Bench Upholds State Sub-Classification of Scheduled Castes Under Article 16(4)
articles.primary_category: Supreme Court Judgments and Important Legal Developments
executive_brief: A 7-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court ruled 6:1 in State of Punjab v.
Davinder Singh that States are constitutionally empowered under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) to sub-classify Scheduled Castes based on empirical data of inadequate representation.
The Court overruled the 2004 E.V.

detailedExplanation: A 7-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court ruled 6:1 in State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh that States are constitutionally empowered under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) to sub-classify Scheduled Castes based on empirical data of inadequate representation.

The Court overruled the 2004 E.V. Chinnaiah judgment which had treated Scheduled Castes as a homogeneous class. The Bench clarified that sub-classification does not tinker with the Presidential Notification under Article 341(1) and requires quantifiable empirical evidence collected by the State.

articles.headline: Census on Foreign Liabilities and Assets of Indian Direct Investment Entities for 2025-26
articles.source_name: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) • Official Releases
executive_brief: Today, the Reserve Bank released the provisional results of the 2025-26 1 round of the annual census on foreign liabilities and assets (FLA) covering cross-border liabilities and assets of the Indian entities [viz., companies, limited liability partnerships (LLPs), alternative investment funds (AIFs) and partnership firms] with inward/outward direct investment.

The FLA census captures detailed information on foreign liabilities and assets in terms of direct investment, portfolio investment and other investments comprising of trade credit, loans, currency & deposits and other payables and receivables accounts, activity sector, sales, purchase, exports, and imports.

The variations in outstanding foreign assets / liabilities between the beginning and end of a financial year would be different from flows recorded in India’s balance of payments (BoP) statistics during the year, as the former would also include valuation changes due to price and exchange rate movements.

detailedExplanation: Today, the Reserve Bank released the provisional results of the 2025-26 1 round of the annual census on foreign liabilities and assets (FLA) covering cross-border liabilities and assets of the Indian entities [viz., companies, limited liability partnerships (LLPs), alternative investment funds (AIFs) and partnership firms] with inward/outward direct investment. The FLA census captures detailed information on foreign liabilities and assets in terms of direct investment, portfolio investment and other investments comprising of trade credit, loans, currency & deposits and other payables and receivables accounts, activity sector, sales, purchase, exports, and imports.

The variations in outstanding foreign assets / liabilities between the beginning and end of a financial year would be different from flows recorded in India’s balance of payments (BoP) statistics during the year, as the former would also include valuation changes due to price and exchange rate movements. Key highlights: Of the total number of Indian entities reporting foreign direct investment (FDI) and/or overseas direct investment (ODI), around 97 per cent entities were unlisted as at end-March 2026, and also held a major share in total FDI equity capital (at face value) in India ( Tables 1 and 2A ). Non-financial companies accounted for more than 90 per cent of the FDI equity at face value ( Table 2B ).

articles.headline: RBI launches the November 2026 round of the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households
articles.source_name: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) • Official Releases
executive_brief: The Reserve Bank of India has been regularly conducting Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH).
The November 2026 round of the survey is being launched.

The survey aims at capturing subjective assessments on price movements and inflation, based on their individual consumption baskets, across 19 cities, viz., Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi and Thiruvananthapuram.

detailedExplanation: The Reserve Bank of India has been regularly conducting Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH). The November 2026 round of the survey is being launched.

The survey aims at capturing subjective assessments on price movements and inflation, based on their individual consumption baskets, across 19 cities, viz., Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi and Thiruvananthapuram. The survey seeks qualitative responses from households on price changes (general prices as well as prices of specific product groups) in the three months ahead as well as in the one year ahead period and quantitative responses on current, three months ahead and one year ahead inflation rates. The results of this survey provide useful inputs for monetary policy.
